sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: 3D space is defined by standard basis vectors.
Each vector is i, j, and k.
Linear transformation moves these basis vectors.

sections.title: The Transformation Matrix
lecture_lines: A matrix stores new vector coordinates.
Column one represents the new i.
Column two represents the new j.
Column three represents the new k.
animations: Animate vector v mapping to M*v in #00FFFF.

sections.title: Visualizing Transformations: Shear and Rotation
lecture_lines: Linear transformations keep the origin fixed.
Grid lines remain straight and parallel.
Rotations and shears are common examples.
animations: Show shear transformation on unit square in #FFA500.
Show rotation transformation by angle theta in #8A2BE2.

sections.title: Determinants and Volume Scaling
lecture_lines: A unit cube changes volume accordingly.
The absolute value shows volume change.
animations: Show scaled area after transformation in #00CED1.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Computer Graphics
lecture_lines: Matrices chain transformations for complex models.
Used extensively in computer graphics engines.
animations: Show vertex transformation using matrices in #7FFF00.
